title: Hand back the very same node

samples.expr: let t = Hashtbl.create 16 in let next = ref 0 in let a = make t next "x" in let b = make t next "x" in string_of_bool (a == b)
samples.label: let t = Hashtbl.create 16 in let next = ref 0 in let a = make t next "x" in let b = make t next "x" in string_of_bool (a == b)

samples.expr: let t = Hashtbl.create 16 in let next = ref 0 in let a = make t next "x" in let b = make t next "y" in Printf.sprintf "%d %d" a.id b.id
samples.label: let t = Hashtbl.create 16 in let next = ref 0 in let a = make t next "x" in let b = make t next "y" in Printf.sprintf "%d %d" a.id b.id

hints: Two lines are wrong. One is on the `Some n` line, the other is something missing after the new node is built.
`{ n with op = op }` builds a copy, and a copy is not `==` to the original. Return `n` itself.
After building the new node, move the counter on with `incr next`, so the next new node gets the next number.

answer.explain: On a hit the reference returns the stored `n` itself, so every caller that asks for the same op holds the very same node and `==` is true. On a miss it builds the node with `id = !next`, runs `incr next` so no two nodes share a number, saves the node in the table and returns it.
